column1: # Host and request target → the Caddyfile path matcher that claims it, or
# "other", as both stats/route.go (Go) and caddylog's route.rs (Rust) must
# answer it. Tab-separated: host, target, route.
# Every matcher in the table has a row, so one going missing fails here.
# The query string is not part of the path.
# The host loses its port and its case.
# An absolute-form target routes by its path; the asterisk and authority
# forms carry no path for a matcher to claim.
# Dot segments pop and doubled slashes collapse before matching.
# A trailing slash survives cleaning, so it is not the exact matcher.
# but a prefix matcher still claims it.
# Percent escapes decode before matching, including an encoded slash.
# A bad escape stays literal rather than failing the target.
# And it does not stop the good escapes decoding: here the good one is
# what reaches the matcher at all.
# Matching is case-insensitive on the path too.
# A host no site serves is route-blind, whatever the path looks like.
# A matcher belongs to its own site: 1d4's own paths are not muchq's.
# Unrouted paths on a served site share one token.
# The matchers the rows above do not reach.
# The FQDN's trailing dot reaches the same vhost, so it folds to the same
# site rather than filing real traffic under the unrouted token.
